text:
dave: Noticed a recurring p99 tail on us-west GPU shelf this morning. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/gpu/us-west-shelf-9 . Top offender looks like tenant `vectorflow` doing heavy KV-cache regen + large PCIe dma ops during init. p50=10ms p95=38ms p99=280-520ms depending on burst. Any quick mitigations?
emma: Oof. Is that thermal/fan or PCIe saturation? can you dump host telemetry for a sample job?
dave: early signs point to PCIe DMA bursts and NIC egress saturation at the top-of-rack. Host logs show repeated PCIe retrain warnings and GPU fan ramp events. Also kvcache miss rate spikes correlate with p99. I can attach a sample trace.
frank: Short-term we could do a soft-pin routing: label a pair of shelves as `heavy-io=true` and steer suspected tenants there with affinity. Apply egress shaping at ToR (10Gbps per tenant) + pcie backpressure mitigation by cgroup throttles. That avoids immediate dedicated capacity while isolating noisy IO.
emma: Prefer trying eBPF-based per-pod egress policing before re-labeling nodes; less disruptive. We have a small eBPF hook that can token-bucket by pod IP. If that reduces p99, we can then add node labels + scheduler rule.
dave: Good call. What's the smallest canary we can run?
frank: Steps: 1) enable eBPF policer on 2 racks (shelf-9a, shelf-9b) 2) tag pods with annotation `io_class=heavy` 3) attach eBPF TBF: rate=9gbit burst=64k 4) add scheduler affinity for `io_class=heavy` fallback to others if oversubscribed 5) collect p50/p95/p99 + pci errors.
emma: eBPF snippet (install via csd): ```bash
# enable policer on ToR
csd apply eBPF-policer --to=tor-shelf-9 --config '{"rate_gbps":9,"burst_kb":64}'
# annotate pod
kubectl annotate pod <pod> io_class=heavy --overwrite
```
infra-bot: alert: us-west/shelf-9 p99 > 300ms for 16m  suspected_tag=\"vectorflow\". Recommendation: run eBPF canary; schedule retention window 24h.
dave: Cost note: if we carve dedicated racks (soft reserve) that's ~6 GPUs * 2 racks -> ~$1.8k/week at current rates, plus potential egress bills if saturated. eBPF route is nearly zero infra cost.
frank: Rollout plan: run eBPF canary for 24h; if p99 for non-heavy pods drops >=40% and pci retrain events fall, we promote to label+softpin for 72h. Rollback: remove eBPF policer and annotations, then revert scheduler.
emma: I'll own canary deployment and metrics dashboard; dave you watch thermal/pci logs; frank you handle scheduler patch if we go next step. Also add trace hook for kvcache hit/miss every 5m.
dave: Will add KV-cache probe and flash a packet-capture on ToR for 1h after rule applied. Abort if p95 for shared slices increases by >10%.
frank: Commands I'll use to label nodes if needed: ```bash
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l shelf=shelf-9 -o name | head -n 8); do
  kubectl label $n heavy_io=true --overwrite
done
# scheduler affinity patch
kubectl patch deployment proxy --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"scheduler.alpha.kubernetes.io/affinity":"..."}}}}}'
```
emma: Starting canary at 02:30 UTC; infra-bot will post updates. Please keep messages short here and dump raw traces to the canary run thread. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: info: eBPF canary started by emma at 6112345800, run_id=ebpf-canary-6112. Will post aggregated metrics every 10m.
dave: Thanks. If this works we should add an automated detection rule to mark high-io tenants and pre-assign them to shield shelves during nightly heavy windows.
emma: Agreed. Also will draft a short playbook for cleanup and cost calc after 24h.
frank: One more ask: capture PCIe error counts per host pre/post. If retrain events persist even after egress shaping, we may need firmware/driver follow-up.
dave: noted. closing thread for now; will reopen with canary results.
